set.st: George Gehrlach, who had lived like the poorest people in a humble cottage on North Cass Street, Portage, died on Saturday evening 13 June 1903. His daughters, Mrs. Paulina Felgenheuer and Mrs. Rebecca Manthey, claimed $6,000-7,000 in notes and mortgages and said the widow had appropriated it, and demanded a warrant. On 16 June Justice Heidt and District Attorney Andrews made an official search and dug up $4,890 in gold under the residence; the wire copies put the money under the kitchen floor at $5,450 with two notes from the daughters. Over $6,000 in property was recovered in all, and a bitter estate fight followed. The widow, Magdalena Gehrlach, lived on in Portage's Fifth Ward and left for Germany in 1904; the fight reported in 1903 does not reappear in the later papers. Recovered by the estate; urban lot, no house number printed.
